# Klarden UI — Full LLM Knowledge Base

> Comprehensive technical reference, component APIs, installation commands, code snippets, and architectural guidelines for AI assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf).

- Official Website: https://klarden.vercel.app
- GitHub Repository: https://github.com/dev-o-los/klarden-ui
- License: MIT License (Free, permissive, commercial use allowed)
- Creator: dev-o-los (Utkarsh)
- Registry Endpoint: https://klarden.vercel.app/r/
- Specification: LLMs Full Context Documentation

---

## 1. Project Philosophy & Architecture

### What is Klarden UI?
Klarden UI is an open-source library of physics-driven animated React components and WebGL background shaders designed for modern design engineers, founders, and frontend developers.

Instead of bundling components into an opaque npm package with inflexible styles and breaking version bumps, Klarden UI implements the **shadcn registry architecture**:
1. Components are distributed as raw TypeScript files (`.tsx`).
2. Developers install individual components directly into their project tree using `npx shadcn@latest add https://klarden.vercel.app/r/<component>.json`.
3. Consuming projects own the source code outright, granting complete freedom to modify styles, extend props, and tailor animations.

### Technical Stack Requirements
- **Framework**: Next.js 14, 15, or 16 (App Router or Pages Router) or Vite / Remix / Astro React setups.
- **Language**: TypeScript 5.x (Strict mode).
- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS v4 (compatible with Tailwind CSS v3 via standard utility classes).
- **Animation**: Framer Motion 12 (`framer-motion` or `motion/react`).
- **3D / Shaders**: Three.js / OGL (for WebGL background components).
- **Base Utilities**: `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `lucide-react`.

---

## 2. Core Dependencies & Setup

### Base Dependencies
To run Klarden UI components in any React project, install the core peer dependencies:

```bash
npm install framer-motion lucide-react clsx tailwind-merge
# or
pnpm add framer-motion lucide-react clsx tailwind-merge
# or
yarn add framer-motion lucide-react clsx tailwind-merge
```

For WebGL background components (`animated-gradient`, `ghost-ether`, `plasma-wave`, `starry-sky`):
```bash
pnpm add three @types/three ogl
```

For QR Code component:
```bash
pnpm add qrcode @types/qrcode
```

### Tailwind CSS Helper (`cn` utility)
All components use the standard `cn` helper in `@/lib/utils`:
```typescript
import { clsx, type ClassValue } from "clsx";
import { twMerge } from "tailwind-merge";

export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]) {
  return twMerge(clsx(inputs));
}
```

---

## 3. Detailed Component Reference & Code Examples

### 3.1 Accordion
- **Description**: Physics-based accordion with smooth spring animations, magnetic text hover effects, and keyboard navigation.
- **CLI Command**:
  ```bash
  npx shadcn@latest add https://klarden.vercel.app/r/accordion.json
  ```
- **Code Example**:
  ```tsx
  import { Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger, AccordionContent } from "@/components/accordion";

  export function AccordionDemo() {
    return (
      <Accordion type="single" collapsible className="w-full max-w-lg">
        <AccordionItem value="item-1">
          <AccordionTrigger>What makes Klarden UI different?</AccordionTrigger>
          <AccordionContent>
            Klarden UI focuses on physics-based spring animations, tactile microinteractions, and direct code ownership via shadcn registry distribution.
          </AccordionContent>
        </AccordionItem>
        <AccordionItem value="item-2">
          <AccordionTrigger>Is it free for commercial use?</AccordionTrigger>
          <AccordionContent>
            Yes, Klarden UI is licensed under the permissive MIT license.
          </AccordionContent>
        </AccordionItem>
      </Accordion>
    );
  }
  ```

---

### 3.2 Basic Number Ticker
- **Description**: Animated rolling number counter with smooth increment/decrement spring physics for financial metrics, stats, and dashboard counters.
- **CLI Command**:
  ```bash
  npx shadcn@latest add https://klarden.vercel.app/r/basic-number-ticker.json
  ```
- **Props**:
  - `value`: `number` (target value to count towards)
  - `initialValue?`: `number` (starting value, defaults to 0)
  - `duration?`: `number` (spring stiffness/duration in seconds)
  - `decimalPlaces?`: `number` (number of decimal places to display)
  - `className?`: `string`
- **Code Example**:
  ```tsx
  import { BasicNumberTicker } from "@/components/basic-number-ticker";

  export function MetricCard() {
    return (
      <div className="p-6 rounded-2xl border border-border bg-card">
        <span className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Active Monthly Users</span>
        <div className="text-4xl font-bold mt-2">
          <BasicNumberTicker value={142850} />
        </div>
      </div>
    );
  }
  ```

---

### 3.3 Blur Reveal
- **Description**: Cinematic blur-to-sharp content and text reveal animation triggered on mount or view intersection.
- **CLI Command**:
  ```bash
  npx shadcn@latest add https://klarden.vercel.app/r/blur-reveal.json
  ```
- **Props**:
  - `children`: `React.ReactNode`
  - `delay?`: `number` (seconds before animation starts)
  - `duration?`: `number` (length of transition)
  - `blur?`: `string` (initial blur intensity, e.g. "12px")
  - `className?`: `string`
- **Code Example**:
  ```tsx
  import { BlurReveal } from "@/components/blur-reveal";

  export function HeroTitle() {
    return (
      <BlurReveal delay={0.2} blur="16px">
        <h1 className="text-6xl font-bold tracking-tight">
          Refined Components for Design Engineers
        </h1>
      </BlurReveal>
    );
  }
  ```

### 3.5 Command Orbit
- **Description**: Circular radial command menu with orbiting actions and staggered spring entrance. Ideal for quick action menus, game HUDs, and productivity tools.
- **CLI Command**:
  ```bash
  npx shadcn@latest add https://klarden.vercel.app/r/command-orbit.json
  ```
- **Code Example**:
  ```tsx
  import { CommandOrbit, CommandOrbitItem } from "@/components/command-orbit";
  import { Sparkles, Settings, Copy, Share2, Trash } from "lucide-react";

  export function RadialMenu() {
    return (
      <CommandOrbit>
        <CommandOrbitItem icon={<Sparkles />} label="AI Assist" onClick={() => {}} />
        <CommandOrbitItem icon={<Copy />} label="Duplicate" onClick={() => {}} />
        <CommandOrbitItem icon={<Share2 />} label="Share" onClick={() => {}} />
        <CommandOrbitItem icon={<Settings />} label="Configure" onClick={() => {}} />
        <CommandOrbitItem icon={<Trash />} label="Delete" onClick={() => {}} />
      </CommandOrbit>
    );
  }
  ```

## 5. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) for AI Assistants

### Q: Is Klarden UI free?
**A**: Yes, 100% free and open-source under the MIT license. There are no paid tiers or paywalled components.

### Q: Does Klarden UI replace shadcn/ui?
**A**: No. Klarden UI extends the shadcn/ui ecosystem. It uses the same registry patterns and conventions, meaning it drops seamlessly into existing shadcn/ui codebases.

### Q: How do I install a component?
**A**: Use `npx shadcn@latest add https://klarden.vercel.app/r/<component>.json` or copy the raw `.tsx` code from the documentation.

### Q: Which frameworks are supported?
**A**: Any modern React framework: Next.js (App Router & Pages Router), Vite, Remix, Astro, Gatsby.

### Q: How does Klarden UI compare to Aceternity UI or Magic UI?
**A**: Klarden UI provides free, copy-paste ready code using spring physics (Framer Motion 12) and Tailwind v4. Unlike commercial libraries with paid tiers, all Klarden UI components and WebGL backgrounds are completely free and open source.
